source.title: Better Language Models Exhibit Higher Visual Alignment
source.authors: Jona Ruthardt; G. Burghouts; Serge J. Belongie; Yuki M. Asano

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests visual alignment using zero-shot classification on unaligned concepts and reports how performance varies with language-model capability, model size, and representation inputs. This is a different measure from direct comparisons of representational distances.
record.gate_note: The main alignment measure is classification accuracy after learning a projection of language features into a frozen vision model's feature space, not a direct comparison of distances between independently trained models. Rows cover the principal visual-generalization results in Table 1, the controlled size/objective comparison in Table 13, and the fine-tuning comparison in Table 8. ShareLock downstream benchmark results are not rows: they primarily evaluate the proposed VLM rather than convergence itself.
record.test_reason: The study maps frozen language-model features into a frozen DINOv2 space with a linear projection. It scores alignment by zero-shot accuracy on classes disjoint from training, then relates that score to language-model capability (MMLU-Pro r=0.768) and size (matched-data Ettin series). This is a different method aimed at the PRH cross-modal question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that text-only LLMs carry non-trivial visual alignment and that this alignment correlates with language capability (MMLU-Pro, r=0.768). Decoders beat encoders even at matched data and size. The base model's pretraining matters more than post-hoc fine-tuning. They use these findings to build ShareLock, a data-efficient frozen-backbone VLM.
record.recipe_differences: Uses learned projections and zero-shot classification accuracy on disjoint concepts as a proxy for cross-modal alignment, rather than directly comparing representational distance matrices. Projections are trained using aligned supervision; the vision backbone is generally frozen.
record.method_sensitivity: Visual generalization varies with the textual class representation (class names, generated Wikipedia-style articles, or Wikipedia articles) and, in the Ettin comparison, decoder pooling (average versus last token). Results also vary across model families and fine-tuning regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning effects on visual alignment. Llama-3 8B drops from 44.4 to 42.7 after instruction tuning and to 34.0 after visual (LLaVA) tuning. Qwen2, Vicuna and Phi-3 shift by under 2 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc instruction or multimodal fine-tuning of an LLM does not reliably increase, and can decrease, its alignment with a vision model's space.

fits_no_version.finding: With matched data and size (Ettin), decoder (next-token) LMs align with DINOv2 about 2.7 pp better than encoder (masked) LMs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining objective affects cross-modal alignment at fixed data and size.

record.problems: The primary alignment outcome is downstream classification accuracy after a learned projection, not a direct geometric similarity measure. Most language-model comparisons differ in pretraining objectives, datasets, and parameter counts; the authors explicitly note that architectural effects cannot generally be isolated. The controlled Ettin comparison addresses matched data and size but is limited to that family. Reported correlations are not causal, and several results aggregate over four datasets and five seeds without uncertainty shown in Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: None; fewer than 60 rows were included.

untested.parts: No direct representational similarity metric. Only one vision model in the probe, so no convergence among many independently trained models of varied architecture, objective and data.
Only the language side is scaled in the strict probe; the vision model is fixed (DINOv2-L). Joint improvement of both models is not tested there.
Entire version: projection seeds are varied, but no comparison of independently initialized backbones.
A linear map from text to vision enables zero-shot transfer, but mapping loss is never quantified. Stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping are not tested.
Alternative similarity metrics and their settings (e.g., kNN k), and out-of-distribution image inputs in the probe.
Completeness or plateau of alignment, and a causal test of shared data or objectives versus a common model of reality. Only an authors' speculation about Phi-3 data curation is offered.

missing.what: Within-family size scaling of visual generalization (class names). Qwen2 0.5B→7B: 29.4→39.1. Qwen2.5 0.5B→32B: 30.6→43.7, non-monotone (7B 40.9, 14B 41.4). gemma-2 2B→9B: 39.1→43.5. Llama-3.2 1B→3B: 35.3→37.8. Falcon3 1B→10B: 33.8→43.0. Phi-3 mini→medium: ~30→34.3.
CLIP ViT-B/16 text encoder reference score of 46.7 vs best unimodal Gemma-2 9B at 44.9. This puts LM alignment near, but below, a vision-trained text encoder.
Additional Table 11 models not rowed: Llama-3.1 8B, Gemma 7B, and the T5-3b vs SentenceT5 naming. Also per-dataset results with seed SDs.
Vision-side scaling. Swapping DINOv2-S/B/L/G in ShareLock raises downstream ImageNet accuracy 45.6→52.1→54.5→56.3, leveling off at Giant. This is a downstream task, not the strict disjoint probe.
Mapping direction asymmetry: projecting vision into the language space consistently underperforms language into vision.

record.verdict_notes: The alignment measure is accuracy after a learned linear projection, a proxy rather than a geometric similarity. It is fitted with class-level supervision on disjoint concepts. Only the language model varies in the probe; DINOv2-L is fixed. ShareLock benchmark tables (2–5, 9–10) evaluate the proposed method and are correctly excluded as rows. The Phi-3 data-curation explanation is the authors' speculation ('likely') and does not test V7. The record's claim that V4 is tested is overstated, since mapping loss is never measured.

versions.untested_parts: Does not directly measure representational distances or establish convergence across independently trained models with systematically varied architectures, objectives, and datasets. Joint scaling of vision and language model size is not tested.
Uses a fixed DINOv2-L vision backbone and learned projections; it does not jointly scale both modalities or directly measure distances between paired images and captions.
No comparison of independently initialized seeds for shared features or subspaces.

Tests learned projection of language features into vision space for classification, but does not measure representation-preservation loss, stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified across models.

Varies textual class representations and pooling in some experiments, but does not compare alternative similarity metrics or settings such as neighbour counts. It does not test whether alignment vanishes under other metrics.

Does not establish that shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the alignment. Compositional-task results are not a direct measure of representational convergence.
